content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm working on a project that requires more than 24 digital inputs, so I've added a second [product_name] unit as a slave to accommodate the extra inputs needed. I'm wondering if it's possible to use the remaining inputs (DI 7, 8, 1, and 2) on the slave module as analogue inputs (NAI). After setting up the second unit as a slave, I cannot find the option to enable analogue inputs in its settings. Does this mean it's not feasible, or is there an alternative solution? Sorry if this post belongs in a different thread! Thank you.

Here is a question: Why are you setting up a master-slave arrangement? Why not use a master-master configuration instead? When you set up the slave [product_name] this way, it acts only as a basic hardware extension for the master. Unless you have a specific need for a master-slave setup, I would recommend trying master-master instead.

Hello [user_name], I wasn't aware a master-master connection was possible. Previously, I networked two base units using a master-slave setup, as recommended by local [company_name] support. Quick question: when using a master-slave connection, I only downloaded the program to the master device. Does the same process apply to a master-master connection? Thanks again.

No need to apologize. With a master-master setup, each [product_name] runs its own independent program. They communicate data over the network. Typically, one device acts as a client and the other as a server. Would you like an example?
Hi [user_name], I think I understand, but seeing an example would be very helpful for me, as I learn best that way. Thanks again!

Check out this video from [company_name]—it demonstrates how to network [product_name] devices using drag-and-drop, showing a master-master configuration. Networking [product_name] devices via drag-and-drop.
Yes, I remember now—everything appears green! Thank you.
Glad to hear that! Has this resolved your issue?

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced difficulties enabling additional analogue inputs on a networked [product_name] set as a slave, finding the relevant configuration options unavailable. Advice received initially suggested a master-slave arrangement, which limited access and control over analogue I/O. The community clarified that using a master-master network approach allows both devices to operate with their own programs and access features that are restricted in slave mode. The collaborative discussion led to a successful solution and improved understanding for the user.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hoped to utilize all available analogue inputs on both base units, even when one is set as a slave in a networked system. They also wanted clear, accessible configuration settings within the software.
